solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Very quick sauce absorbing last of powder (6)

indicators.note: the sauce takes the letter into itself
take only the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A cook's sauce thickens fast once the last of some powder is stirred in.
explanation.walkthrough: Presto is the musical marking for a very fast tempo.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto, from Italian, means very quick, especially as a musical direction.

clue.text: Exhausted, Romeo and some others head off (3,3)

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is cut off

blocks.note: SUNDRY (various, some others) losing its first letter

explanation.surface: Romeo and a few companions are worn out and set off.
explanation.walkthrough: Sundry means various or miscellaneous, as in 'all and sundry'; decapitating it leaves UNDRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A supply that has run dry is exhausted, used up entirely.

clue.text: Pan surrounded by principal Caribbean fruit (4,5)

indicators.note: the first word goes inside the second

blocks.note: a staple is a main or principal item
to pan or rap is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: A cooking pan sits in the middle of the main Caribbean fruit display.
explanation.walkthrough: Pan here is a verb, to slate a show; the kitchen pan is the trap.
explanation.definitionFit: The star apple is a tropical fruit native to the Caribbean, named for the star pattern inside when cut.

clue.text: Bugged too much by the rabble, as they say (9)

indicators.note: points to how the word is spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: the herd is the common mob

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed at being pestered too much by the mob.
explanation.walkthrough: Bugged reads as annoyed, but here it means secretly listened to, as with a hidden microphone.
explanation.definitionFit: Speech that is bugged is picked up covertly, that is, overheard.

clue.text: Soft fool left travel document (8)

blocks.note: p for piano, soft in music
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A gentle idiot has forgotten his travel papers.
explanation.walkthrough: Left looks like the past tense of leave, but it is the nautical side.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is the official document needed to travel abroad.

clue.text: Old philosopher concerned with a group of soldiers (7)

explanation.surface: An ancient thinker takes an interest in a unit of troops.
explanation.walkthrough: On is the usual crossword word for 'about' or 'concerning', as in a talk on Plato.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a small military unit of soldiers.

clue.text: Stick with supply (5)

blocks.note: the noun: a long pole or walking stick
the verb: to provide a place with workers

explanation.surface: Stay loyal to a supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: Stick looks like a verb, to stay with, but it is the noun, a long pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff is a stout stick, and to staff a place is to supply it with personnel.

clue.text: Glass of beer encapsulating old location (5)

indicators.note: the glass holds the letter inside it

blocks.note: o is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A pint in an old spot, like a traditional pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Glass of beer is the pint itself, not a drinking vessel in general.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a point on a map is a precise spot or location.

clue.text: Going back greening with motivation (8)

indicators.note: motivation read as motion: the letters are set moving

explanation.surface: Someone backs away from an eco drive despite being keen.
explanation.walkthrough: Reneging is going back on a promise.
explanation.definitionFit: To renege is to go back on a promise or agreement.

clue.text: Being filmed beside judge’s off ice (2,6)

blocks.note: on as in a town on the river, next to it
camera is a judge's private room, as in 'in camera'

explanation.surface: Someone is filmed next to a judge who is stepping off the ice, as at a skating contest.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'off ice' as one word, office: a judge's private chambers are the camera, from which hearings 'in camera' take their name.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a presenter who is on camera is in shot, being recorded.

clue.text: An isle settling foreigners (6)

indicators.note: the letters settle into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Incomers are making their home on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Settling looks like the incomers moving in, but it tells the six letters of 'An isle' to settle into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal sense: in immigration law, a non-citizen resident is termed an alien.

clue.text: Start to speak about British fish (6)

explanation.surface: Someone begins a talk on a British fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole phrase 'Start to speak about', not just 'Start'.
explanation.definitionFit: To broach a subject is to raise it for the first time.

clue.text: Upper-class sorts wither as leader moves away from set (8)

indicators.note: the first letter shifts to a later position

explanation.surface: Posh types fade as their leader departs the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFFSAGE has its leading T moved back to sit after OFFS. Toff is British slang for a posh person.
explanation.definitionFit: Offstage means out of sight of the audience, away from the stage set.

clue.text: Runner is bound to let off pressure (3)

indicators.note: the letter is released and dropped

blocks.note: p is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A sprinter is bound to vent some stress.
explanation.walkthrough: Runner is not an athlete but the blade a sledge slides on; a ski is one.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is a runner, a long narrow strip that slides over snow.

clue.text: Smooth progress intends to take in one in poor health (5,7)

explanation.surface: Someone means to make easy headway while looking after a sick person.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's patient is a trap: 'in poor health' is just a synonym to add, and the only thing taken in is one.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from the sea: a voyage with no hazards, used for any task that goes easily.

clue.text: Perversely ‘lethal’ means entirely (3,3,3)

indicators.note: the letters are twisted into a contrary order

explanation.surface: A quote about something deadly meaning total.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Means' looks like the verb joining the two halves, but it is the noun, a way.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: agreeing with someone all the way is agreeing wholly, without reservation.

clue.text: Lean on press release with cool manufacturer’s suggestion (4,5)

blocks.note: a ship lists when it leans

explanation.surface: A firm leans on a calm press release to push its recommendation.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' says the first piece sits above the next.
explanation.definitionFit: The list price is the price a manufacturer suggests retailers charge.

clue.text: Amazingly I swear it could be a climber (8)

indicators.note: the letters are bewildered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone swears, astonished, that it might be a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: A climber here is a climbing plant, not a mountaineer.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisteria is a climbing plant with hanging clusters of flowers.

clue.text: Possibly this tennis match is suggested by bold Sue (5,7)

blocks.note: the surface reading: a game of tennis, perhaps a particular kind
the setter's reading: the letters of 'bold Sue', once jumbled, spell a word for a two-a-side game

explanation.surface: Sue, a confident player, points to her kind of tennis game.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: 'mixed' letters of BOLD SUE give 'doubles', so the phrase describes itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Mixed doubles is a tennis match with a man and a woman on each side.

clue.text: Cheated Queen of Carthage out of nothing (3)

indicators.note: 'out of nothing' reads as Dido short of an O: she is out of it, the zero no longer there

blocks.note: the legendary queen of Carthage in the Aeneid

explanation.surface: Dido was swindled out of everything.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'do' someone is informal for cheating them, so 'did' is cheated.
explanation.definitionFit: Did, as in 'they did me out of my money', means cheated.

clue.text: Among Germans and therefore stand (7)

explanation.surface: Some Germans, and so they take a stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Among Germans and' means 'and' as Germans say it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'I can't stand it' uses stand as endure, which is what undergoing a trial means.

clue.text: Dad, having been put upon, let up (6)

explanation.surface: A father, having been exploited, eased off.
explanation.walkthrough: Someone put upon has been taken advantage of, that is, used.
explanation.definitionFit: To let up is to pause or stop for a while.

clue.text: Flag policy on a road (8)

blocks.note: a stand is a position or policy

explanation.surface: A plan for marking out a road with a warning signal.
explanation.walkthrough: Flag looks like a verb, to wave or tire, but it is the noun: a standard is a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a flag, especially one carried as an emblem.

clue.text: Belt up then check, obviously (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue, up turns the word backwards

blocks.note: to belt or tan is to beat
then places it next; ch is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: Buckle your seat belt, then check it: obvious advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Belt up' tempts as 'be quiet'; instead belt is TAN, a thrashing, read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Natch is informal shorthand for naturally, meaning obviously.

clue.text: Relatives making visits when husband is out (5)

indicators.note: a husband who is out is not at home, so his letter is absent from the word

blocks.note: to haunt a place is to visit it often

explanation.surface: The in-laws come round when the husband is away.
explanation.walkthrough: Making visits is haunts, to haunt a place being to frequent it, not a noun for the visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: an aunt is one kind of relative, a parent's sister.

clue.text: Bobby is surrounded by passion for old jazz fan (6)

indicators.note: the first word sits inside the second

blocks.note: a bobby is a British police constable

explanation.surface: A policeman is mobbed by admirers of an old-time swing fan.
explanation.walkthrough: Bobby is British slang for a police officer, a PC.
explanation.definitionFit: Hepcat is dated slang for a fan of jazz or swing music.

clue.text: Cheesy dish windin’ you up (6)

indicators.note: the dropped g shows the next word loses its final g too

blocks.note: winding you up means irritating, and dialect drops the final g, as windin' itself does

explanation.surface: A cheesy dish that's getting on your nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in windin' tells you to clip grating the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: A gratin is a dish topped with browned cheese or breadcrumbs.

clue.text: Fixed two rides being most noisy (8)

indicators.note: the letters are repaired into a new order

explanation.surface: Two rigged fairground rides are the loudest.
explanation.walkthrough: Fixed reads as mended or rigged; here it means arranged, telling you to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdiest means the noisiest and most disorderly.

clue.text: Sense of male pride in measure of speed is second (8)

blocks.note: Mach number, speed relative to sound
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A man's pride in how fast he goes comes second.
explanation.walkthrough: Second is not a ranking but a moment, as in 'just a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: A borrowing from Spanish macho: the word names an exaggerated, swaggering masculine pride.

clue.text: Gives up investment returns (6)

blocks.note: a plural noun: the income an investment produces

explanation.surface: An investor surrenders returns.
explanation.walkthrough: Gives up is a verb and investment returns a plural noun; one word covers both.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an army surrenders, yielding ground, and a bond's annual income is its yield.
